title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 47-50): Grothendieck is formulating his 'conjecture fondamentale' of anabelian geometry. It concerns 'modèles élémentaires anabéliens' U, smooth schemes of finite type over Q that are K(pi,1) and built from successive fibrations in hyperbolic curves. Each U has an extension 1 -> pi_U -> E_U -> Gamma_Q -> 1, where pi_U = pi_1(U-bar) is the geometric fundamental group and E_U = pi_1(U). The conjecture is the Hom-form: morphisms of schemes correspond to exterior (outer) homomorphisms of these extensions over Gamma_Q.

On this page he extends the domain of the conjecture from schemes of finite type to pro-schemas. Take V = lim V_i, a limit in the category of schemes of regular, connected schemes of finite type over Q, with affine transition morphisms. A small insertion over the transition maps may read 'immersions ouvertes', i.e. V a localisation. For such V the conjectured statement is: dominant morphisms V -> U correspond to exterior homomorphisms E_V -> E_U over Gamma_Q = E_Q whose image is open. Open image is the group-theoretic counterpart of dominance.

The example he gives is U regular and V = Spec O_{U,x}, the spectrum of the local ring at a point x of U (struck out: Spec(O_{X,x})). These are intermediate objects:
- at the closed points one recovers the section-type statements of the previous page;
- at the generic point one gets the function field, i.e. the 'birational' anabelian statement;
- in between are local rings of arbitrary codimension.
On p. 48 he notes that the conjecture for models implies the conjecture for fields, restricted to suitably compatible loci; this page supplies the pro-scheme formulation that makes the passage work.

Second paragraph (programme). Granting the conjecture, 'possibly revised and corrected along the way', the next problem is to determine which pro-Galois homotopy types over BQ come from elementary anabelian models. Equivalently, the groups pi_U being known, one must determine the possible exterior actions of Gamma_Q (and of inertia-type subgroups, per p. 50) on them. The next page continues with analogous questions for K(pi,1)s realised by non-elementary varieties, notably moduli varieties of curves. It then proposes a gluing ('recollement') reconstruction of the category of smooth schemes over fields of finite type, and over arbitrary fields, via a category of fractions.
errors: No genuine error. The statement is explicitly conjectural and self-flagged as provisional ('revue et corrigée en cours de route').

Gap: the hypotheses on V are left vague. For the Hom-conjecture to be plausible, the finite-type pieces of V (or U) presumably need anabelian/K(pi,1) hypotheses. As written, V is only regular, of finite type, with affine transitions; for the target U the anabelian hypothesis is inherited from context.

Gap: the open-image condition is phrased loosely ('telles que V image soit ouverte'). In later precise versions (letter to Faltings 1983; Mochizuki 1999) the condition is that the homomorphism, or its restriction to geometric pi_1, has open image. Here it is not made precise whether 'open' refers to the image in E_U or in pi_U.

ideas.what: Hom-form anabelian conjecture: dominant morphisms V->U correspond to open exterior homomorphisms E_V -> E_U over Gamma_Q
ideas.modern_name: Hom-version of Grothendieck's anabelian conjecture (dominant maps vs. open homomorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); proved for hyperbolic-curve targets by Mochizuki (1999, sub-p-adic fields)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983); Esquisse d'un programme §3 (more vaguely)

ideas.what: Extending the anabelian correspondence to pro-schemes: limits of regular finite-type Q-schemes, e.g. Spec of local rings O_{U,x}, interpolating between the finite-type case and the function-field (birational) case
ideas.modern_name: anabelian geometry of pro-varieties / local schemes; birational anabelian geometry at the generic point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birational case: Pop (1994 onward), with roots in Neukirch–Uchida; local-ring (non-generic) cases are scarcely treated
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings mentions extension to function fields/birational case; the explicit local-ring formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Programme: classify the pro-Galois types over BQ (exterior Gamma_Q-actions on pi_U) that arise from elementary anabelian models, and analogues for moduli varieties of curves
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme / image of Galois in Out(pi_1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme); developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak, etc.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; La Longue Marche (1981)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly proposes the anabelian Hom-conjecture for spectra of local rings O_{U,x} at arbitrary (non-closed, non-generic) points of anabelian models. This is a 'semi-local' anabelian statement interpolating between section conjecture/points and Pop's birational theorem. It has received little systematic attention compared with the finite-type and birational cases.
missed.quote: P. ex. on pourrait prendre pour (U, ...) réguliers, V = les spectres d'anneaux locaux x ∈ U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A theory of anabelian reconstruction for local schemes Spec O_{U,x} would connect Pop's birational results with Mochizuki's Hom-theorems. It would also support the 'recollement' strategy (reconstructing categories of schemes from local-to-global Galois data) that Grothendieck sketches on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: The Hom-conjecture with open image and the Galois-action programme are known from the letter to Faltings and the Esquisse. The explicit pro-scheme formulation, with spectra of local rings as test objects, is a modestly notable unpublished detail but not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'de type fini' looks like 'immersions ouvertes' rather than 'connexes [?]'. This would make the transition morphisms affine open immersions, consistent with the local-ring example; reading uncertain.
Parenthesis reads roughly '(morphismes de transition affines, sans plus)' (uncertain).
'et telles que V image soit ouverte' should probably read 'et telles que l'image soit ouverte' (open-image condition).
'V = les spectres d'anneaux locaux de U (x ∈ U)': the line 'de type fini sur Q' belongs to the final clause about the schemes U, not V.
